sections.content: How many people stayed in Leeds after gaining qualifications?

Leeds is a city in Yorkshire and The Humber. Leeds also has a university.

Leeds has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Leeds ended up with:

  • more graduates than it produced
  • more non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 20,250 state-school pupils from Leeds who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 5,375 (27%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 5,385 (27%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Leeds to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Leeds' pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Leeds in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Leeds move to?

Of Leeds's graduates, 1,385 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 255 of those graduates (18%) were living fairly locally, in the Leeds travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Leeds's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 965 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 375 of those qualified non-graduates (39%) were living fairly locally, in the Leeds travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Leeds' GCSE cohort:

  • 905 graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 295 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left Yorkshire and The Humber
  • the most common region they moved to was London

In 2018 to 2019, 64% of graduates and 33% of qualified non-graduates living in Leeds had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 10,730 graduates and 6,435 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Leeds. This is compared with the 5,375 graduates and 5,385 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 36% of the graduates had also lived in Leeds as GCSE pupils, while 64% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Leeds in 2018 to 2019, 67% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 33% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
